newsitem.title: USA: Fla. lawmaker seeks to outlaw human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Fla. lawmaker seeks to outlaw human cloning.

text.p: A Florida lawmaker on Friday said he had filed a bill to make human cloning illegal, saying the practice could create a Frankenstein-type monster.
Representative J. Alex Villalobos, a Miami Republican, filed a bill to make it a first-degree felony punishable by up to 30 years in prison for anyone to clone or attempt to clone a human being.
"Technology is moving ahead more rapidly than we can respond to it," Villalobos said. "All I want to do is put the brakes on this until we study it further."

The bill followed a report that a team of Scottish researchers had cloned a sheep. "They applied gentle pulses of electricity. The pulses promoted the egg to accept the nuclei and all the DNA as if it were its own," Villalobos said. "If this isn't Frankenstein, I don't know what is."

John Teem, a researcher studying cystic fibrosis at Florida State University, said the bill could interfere with important medical research as researchers who have nothing to do with human cloning routinely clone portions of DNA strands. "If the law outlaws the use of DNA for that reason it would be making illegal all the research that is being done right now," he said.
There was no indication on Friday of the measure's chances of being passed into law.
